SMTO-GML-0019 — SMTO couldn't connect your Gmail account

GUID: be9a6b65-4dba-4ddc-a5f0-bd8f9717565c
Slug: gmail-not-authorized
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to connect to your Gmail account, but the Google sign-in was cancelled or didn't finish properly, so SMTO has no permission to use the account. Nothing was saved and no emails were touched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, ask SMTO to connect your Gmail account, then select Open authorization page or the Google link it gives you. Each connection attempt starts a new Google sign-in, which replaces the one that failed.
  2. On the Google page, pick the Gmail account you want SMTO to use and select Allow; don't close the window or select Cancel. Cancelling or closing the Google page is the most common reason no permission reaches SMTO.
  3. Wait for the page that says the account is connected and that you can close the window. That message means SMTO received and saved the permission.
  4. If Google shows an error page instead of the Allow screen, select Copy error details here and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Google's app settings for SMTO may need to be fixed by the person who set it up.

What success looks like

  • The Google window says your account is connected and you can close it, and SMTO can now read your Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste your Google password or any sign-in codes into a conversation or a screenshot.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail Google sign-in did not yield a usable account: consent was cancelled, the callback had no valid code, the token exchange or profile lookup failed, no access token was returned, or Gmail returned an empty mailbox address.

What this means

  • OAuth is cancelled or lacks a valid code/access token, token exchange/profile verification fails, or the returned mailbox identity is empty. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth is cancelled or lacks a valid code/access token, token exchange/profile verification fails, or the returned mailbox identity is empty.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the authorization stage and intended account; this family does not prove a wrong password.

How to fix it

  • BrowserOAuth.finish/GmailOAuth.complete raise gmail_not_authorized on a provider error parameter (authorization_cancelled), a missing or oversize code, a failed code exchange or users/me/profile call, or an empty emailAddress; GmailParameterProfiles.save_tokens raises it when no access_token is returned. Check the Gmail OAuth App parameter (client ID/secret, redirect URI, scopes) in Parameter Store and the Server log, then start a fresh gmail.connect flow.
  • Complete supported OAuth authorization for the intended account.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported consent flow verifies the intended mailbox and saves its revision-bound credentials.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
